solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old Sierra Ford, roomy, transporting Pound (a great poet)

parts.note: Sierra is the NATO alphabet code word for S
a Ford is a make of car

indicators.note: transporting means carrying inside, so the word for roomy holds the pound sign letter

parts.note: roomy means wide
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A spacious old Sierra, a Ford model, gives a lift to the poet Ezra Pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' and 'Ford' look like a single car model; they are split, Sierra giving S and Ford giving CAR. 'Pound' looks like Ezra Pound but is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish writer of The Importance of Being Earnest also wrote celebrated verse such as The Ballad of Reading Gaol.

clue.text: Hollow, faint pulse regularly taken

parts.note: faint means dim, as in a faint light

indicators.note: regularly taken means every other letter of pulse is picked, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A weak heartbeat found in a hollow, as a medic might note.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hollow in the cheek or chin is the classic example of this feature.

clue.text: Swiss speciality car rolled, upsetting German driver (5 down)

indicators.note: a rolled car has turned over, so the word car is read backwards
upsetting in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards
5 down here is not a cross-reference: the Roman numeral for five is taken down, removed

parts.note: Sebastian Vettel is a German Formula One champion driver
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A car flips over and upsets a German driver, apparently the one at 5 down.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(5 down)' poses as a cross-reference to another clue; 'down' drops the Roman numeral for five, and 'upsetting' turns the remaining ETTEL upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: This melted-cheese dish, scraped onto potatoes, is a famous Swiss Alpine meal.

clue.text: Hirsute chap's son taking a dip in water in Dieppe

indicators.note: taking a dip in means going into the water, so the son letter sits inside the French word

parts.note: eau is French for water, Dieppe being a French port

explanation.surface: A hairy man's boy goes swimming in the sea at Dieppe.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Jacob's twin brother is described as a hairy man, unlike smooth-skinned Jacob.

clue.text: NaHCO 3 an ingredient of Nacho?

definitions.meaning: the chemical formula for sodium bicarbonate, used as a raising agent
the formula's letters NaHCO rearrange to spell Nacho, so the compound is playfully an ingredient of it

explanation.surface: A chemistry question: is this sodium compound found in Mexican snacks?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a joke: the symbols Na, H, C, O are the letters of NACHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium bicarbonate is the household raising agent sold for cakes and bread.

clue.text: University controlled American body in space

parts.note: controlled means ran, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A university controlled a US space agency, perhaps, overseeing some body.
explanation.definitionFit: The seventh planet from the Sun is a heavenly body orbiting in the solar system.

clue.text: Ask again about Fat Man's goal

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the first two words are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks again about the aim of an overweight man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat Man' looks like a person; it was the codename of the atomic bomb dropped in August 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese city was the target of the Fat Man atomic bomb in the Second World War.

clue.text: Muscle contracted on King Gregory?

indicators.note: contracted means shortened, so the muscle's name is cut to its familiar gym abbreviation

parts.note: a pectoral is a chest muscle
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A flexed muscle on a king named Gregory.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: Gregory is a first name to be completed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood actor of To Kill a Mockingbird was named Gregory, so the surname completes him.

clue.text: One might wind up this actress as April 1 lark!

indicators.note: a lark is a bit of fooling about, so the letters are played with into a new order

parts.note: the figure 1 looks like the letter I, as in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fooling an actress on April Fool's Day, a lark to wind her up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind up' looks like teasing, matching the April Fool prank, but it means climbing round and round.
explanation.definitionFit: A helical flight of steps is climbed by winding round its central column.

clue.text: Horrify adult resident of N Scandinavia heading west

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means going right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Lapp is one of the Sami people of northern Scandinavia

explanation.surface: A grown-up from the Arctic north travelling westward horrifies someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to shock or dismay deeply.

clue.text: Standard trade association card

parts.note: a union is an association of workers in a trade
a jack is a court card, the knave

explanation.surface: A routine membership card from a trade body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like an adjective meaning ordinary; it is the noun, a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The British national flag is a standard, a banner flown as an emblem.

clue.text: Putting up a fight with Sterling playing

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are in play, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Resisting while the pound sterling is behaving badly on the markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappling with an opponent is a literal way of struggling against them.

clue.text: Where solvers are encouraged to seek counsel?

definitions.text: Where solvers are encouraged to seek counsel?

parts.words: Where solvers are encouraged to seek counsel?
parts.note: solvers sounds like problem-solvers, and counsel is a barrister, who sees clients in private rooms; the phrase also means in private

explanation.surface: A puzzle-page tip about where to go for advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Barristers' offices are called chambers; 'counsel' means a barrister as well as advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hearing a matter privately, or a barrister in their offices, is said to sit in this place.

clue.text: Small stringed instrument not perfectly tuned

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A little string instrument that is slightly out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A note pitched slightly too high is off, failing to be exactly in tune.

clue.text: Those buying tea consumed by ships' officers

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed, so the tea word goes inside the officers word

parts.note: pursers are the officers in charge of a ship's accounts
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Those buying tea that ship's officers drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyers are customers who acquire goods in exchange for money.

clue.text: Left, waving "au revoir, Nice" le superstar de Cannes?

indicators.note: waving suggests movement to and fro, so the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A star leaves Cannes, waving and saying goodbye to Nice, in mock French.
explanation.walkthrough: The French words make it sound like a French star; the question mark admits he was English, though his surname sounds French.
explanation.definitionFit: The great English actor of Henry V and Hamlet had a French-sounding surname, hence a cheeky film-festival star.

clue.text: Something to keep you dry? Let me see, Brother Fitzgerald

parts.note: um is the hesitation sound made while thinking, like let me see
Ella Fitzgerald was the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: Someone muses about what keeps you dry, then names a brother called Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: A folding canopy carried overhead shelters a person from rain.

clue.text: Island mansion being renovated — the cause of long, exhausting nights

definitions.text: the cause of long, exhausting nights

indicators.note: being renovated means made over, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Renovating an island mansion keeps the owner awake through long nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Chronic sleeplessness leaves a person lying awake all night and worn out.

clue.text: One raked by fire?

parts.note: raked by fire sounds like coming under gunfire, but a poker rakes through the glowing remains in a grate

explanation.surface: A soldier sprayed by enemy gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raked by fire' suggests a soldier under machine-gun fire; read literally, it is a glowing coal raked out beside a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing fragment left in a dying fire is what gets raked over in the hearth.

clue.text: River mammal — basically a rat

parts.note: an otter is a riverside mammal

explanation.surface: A riverbank animal that is, at bottom, really a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a scoundrel a rat is an insult; this old-fashioned word means the same kind of cad.

clue.text: Pah! Tim's mad — angry, reactionary, grasping Scottish economist

indicators.note: reactionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
grasping means holding inside, so the run of words holds the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that Tim is furious and reactionary, a greedy economist.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'grasping' as part of the definition; it is the indicator that the words hold the letters, without which nothing signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Wealth of Nations was an eighteenth-century Scot, the founder of modern economics.

clue.text: Smitten, I have contracted to cover Nelson occasionally

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap around, so the contraction encloses the picked letters

parts.note: I've is the contraction of I have

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of Nelson is taken

explanation.surface: Infatuated, I caught something while protecting Nelson now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracted' looks like catching a disease, fitting 'Smitten', but it means shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smitten means being struck with romantic infatuation for someone.

clue.text: Weak power — battery unfortunately died

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogy

explanation.surface: The power is low: the battery has sadly gone flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something poor or of low quality can be called weak, as in a weak performance.

clue.text: Leaders of punk's oldest groups organised a dance

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters, taken from each of the next four words

explanation.surface: The first punk bands organised a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly the definition is the jumping dance of punk gigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping straight up and down on the spot is the punk-era dance named after a sprung stick toy.

clue.text: Daughter consumed fruit

parts.note: consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A girl ate a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet brown fruit of a palm tree is a familiar example of fruit.

clue.text: British inventor of bomb factories

definitions.meaning: William ... designed the ... bomb, the British hand grenade of the First World War
a plural noun: works where goods are processed, such as cotton or paper works

explanation.surface: A British engineer who invented a bomb-making plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial works such as textile or flour plants are named for their machinery, and the grenade bears its inventor's surname.

clue.text: One in mourning embraces aged, retired man's best friend

indicators.note: embraces means holds inside, so the mourner word wraps the others

parts.note: a griever is one who mourns
olden means old, of times long ago

explanation.surface: A mourner hugs an old, retired man, his dog at his side.
explanation.definitionFit: This popular gun-dog breed is a dog, and dogs are proverbially humanity's closest companion.
